overview: The Britannica entry conflates Nazarite with Nazarene and Nazarene with Jesus, while the Wikipedia article focuses on the biblical nazirite vow and its rules, history, and later interpretations.

differences.britannica: The entry treats Nazarite, Nazarene, and Nazarene as terms for natives of Nazareth, Jesus, heretics, and vow-takers.
differences.wikipedia: The article defines a nazirite as someone who voluntarily took the vow described in Numbers 6:1–21.

britannica.quote: NAZARITE, or NAZAREAN, or Nazarene, a term which signifies one who is of Nazareth, or any native of the city of Nazareth.

wikipedia.quote: In the Hebrew Bible, a nazirite or a nazarite (Hebrew: נָזִיר Nāzīr) is an Israelite man or woman who voluntarily took a vow which is described in Numbers 6:1–21.

differences.britannica: The entry does not list the specific requirements of the Nazarite vow.
differences.wikipedia: The vow requires abstaining from grape products, not cutting hair, and avoiding contact with corpses.

britannica.quote: one who has laid himself under the obligation of a vow to observe the rules of Nazariteship

wikipedia.quote: Abstain from wine and strong drink as well as all other grape products, such as vinegar

differences.britannica: It states the name Nazarene belongs to Jesus because he lived at Nazareth and the prophets foretold he would be called a Nazarene.
differences.wikipedia: It says Jesus was reportedly a wine-drinker, making it doubtful he was a nazirite during his ministry.

britannica.quote: The name of Nazarene belongs to Jesus Christ, not only because of his having lived the greater part of his life at Nazareth

wikipedia.quote: makes it doubtful that he, reported to be "winedrinker" (Greek οἰνοπότης, oinopotēs), was a nazirite during his ministry

differences.britannica: It names Samson and John the Baptist as lifelong Nazarites.
differences.wikipedia: It names Samson and Samuel as lifelong nazirites, and discusses John the Baptist separately.

britannica.quote: whether it be for his whole life, as Samson and John the Baptist

wikipedia.quote: Two prominent Biblical individuals who were nazirites, or similar to nazirites, were Samson (Judges 13:5), and Samuel (1 Samuel 1:11).

differences.britannica: The entry mentions a meaning of Nazarite as a man of distinction in a prince's court.
differences.wikipedia: The article details Mishna, Talmud, Maimonides, and permanent versus temporary nazirite vows under Jewish law.

britannica.quote: denotes a man of particular distinction and great dignity in the court of some prince.

wikipedia.quote: An Israelite (not a gentile) becomes a Nazirite through an intentional verbal declaration.
